sentence: Stress is a reaction to mental or emotional pressure that can affect mood, body and behaviour; the NHS suggests a GP or NHS 111 when it affects daily life.
note: Stress is usually a reaction to mental or emotional pressure; contact NHS 111 or talk to a GP if affecting daily life

sentence: The NHS describes stress as usually a reaction to mental or emotional pressure, often linked to feeling a loss of control.
note: Stress is usually a reaction to mental or emotional pressure, related to feeling losing control

sentence: Stress can show up as emotional changes, physical symptoms such as headaches and stomach problems, and changes in behaviour.
note: Emotional, physical, behaviour changes

sentence: Long-term or severe stress can lead to exhaustion of body, mind and emotions, often called burnout.
note: Long-term stress can lead to burnout

sentence: Adults in England can refer themselves to NHS Talking Therapies without seeing a GP.
note: Refer yourself directly to NHS Talking Therapies without talking to a GP

sentence: The NHS describes stress as usually a reaction to mental or emotional pressure, often related to feeling a loss of control over something, though sometimes there is no obvious cause.
note: Stress is usually a reaction to mental or emotional pressure; often related to feeling like losing control; sometimes no obvious cause

sentence: Common triggers it lists include pressure at work, relationship or family difficulties, money worries, illness and bereavement.
note: Work, family, financial problems, health, bereavement

sentence: Stress can be useful in small doses, but the NHS says it can become a problem when it is constant.
note: If you're stressed all the time it can become a problem

sentence: Long-term or severe stress can lead to physical, mental and emotional exhaustion, often called burnout.
note: Long-term or severe stress can lead to feeling physical, mental, emotional exhaustion, burnout

sentence: The NHS says stress can affect emotions, causing irritability, anger, tearfulness, worry and feeling overwhelmed.
note: Emotional: irritable, angry, tearful

sentence: Physical symptoms listed include stomach problems, stress headaches, muscle pain, rashes and dizziness.
note: Physical symptoms: stomach problems, headaches, muscle pain, rashes, dizziness

sentence: The NHS also says stress can raise blood pressure or cause chest pains, which should ease once the stress does.
note: Stress can raise blood pressure or cause chest pains, should ease once stress does

sentence: Behaviour can change too, with sleeping too much or too little, eating more or less, avoiding people or places, or drinking or smoking more.
note: Sleeping too much or too little, eating differently, avoiding places or people, drinking or smoking more

sentence: NHS pages suggest identifying the cause as the first step, then breaking large tasks into small targets and focusing on what can be changed.
note: First step to feeling better is to identify the cause; set small targets

sentence: Controlled breathing, deep muscle relaxation and mindful breathing are listed as ways to reduce tension and some of the physical signs of stress.
note: Controlled breathing, deep muscle relaxation, mindful breathing reduce tension

sentence: Talking to trusted friends, family or colleagues, or contacting a helpline, is also suggested.
note: Trusted friends, family, colleagues or helpline can help

sentence: Short CBT-based videos and guides are offered to work through problems in new ways and build resilience.
note: Videos and practical guides to CBT help deal with stress and build resilience

sentence: The NHS advises against using alcohol, cigarettes, gambling or drugs to relieve stress, because these can contribute to poor mental health.
note: Try not to use alcohol, cigarettes, gambling or drugs to relieve stress

sentence: If stress is affecting daily life, the NHS suggests contacting NHS 111 or talking to a GP.
note: If stress is affecting your daily life, contact NHS 111 or talk to a GP

sentence: In England, adults aged 18 and over can refer themselves directly to NHS Talking Therapies without seeing a GP, and in some areas the minimum age is 16.
note: If 18 or over (or 16 or over in some areas) you can refer yourself directly

sentence: If stress has led to thoughts of self-harm or suicide, call 999 if there is immediate danger, use NHS 111 and choose the mental health option for urgent help, or contact Samaritans free at any time on 116 123.
note: Thoughts of harming yourself: see doctor as soon as possible; Samaritans 24-hour help line; 999/111/116 123 per site rule

sentence: An NHS self-help guide describes stress as the body's reaction to feeling under threat, known as the fight or flight response, and says a certain amount of pressure can be helpful and motivating.
note: Stress is body's reaction to feeling under threat; fight or flight; a certain amount of pressure can be helpful and motivating

sentence: The British Heart Foundation explains that the brain signals the body to release hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol.
note: Brain sends signals to body to release hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol

sentence: It says that if this response keeps being switched on again and again, over time it can take its toll on the body.
note: If fight or flight response keeps being switched on again and again, can take its toll on body

sentence: The NHS guide says stress that continues and is not managed can be bad for health.
note: If stress continues and is not managed can be really bad for health
